multibayes

multibayes provides tools for making directional claims about many parameters from posterior draws. Direction-agnostic and directional tests are supported, and can be mixed freely within a single call.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mar-cald/multibayes")

Overview

Function Input What it returns
pd.adjust() Posterior draws or pd vector Prior-odds threshold c* for the probability of direction (per test)
joint() Posterior draws Joint probability of the strongest directional claims (default) or simultaneous credible intervals (interval = TRUE)

pd.adjust() asks for a single quantity, pi0: an upper bound, set by you, on the prior probability of the sign opposite to the claimed one. Because the same pi0 is used for every parameter, it is also an upper bound on the expected proportion of parameters in the family that are not on the claimed side, null effects included, so a judgment about how many null effects the family could contain can guide its choice. Alternatively, p0 is the largest prior probability that no claim in the family is correct, with pi0 = p0^(1/m) for m tests that are independent a priori, so that pi0 grows with the number of tests. A claim is made only if it holds under every prior that lowers the prior odds of either direction by up to pi0/(1 - pi0), which raises the threshold on pd from c (default 0.975) to c*.

library(multibayes)
draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(4000, mu = c(1, 0.2, 3), Sigma = diag(3))
colnames(draws) <- c("b1", "b2", "b3")
pd.adjust(draws = draws, pi0 = 0.7)   # claim a direction when pd.adj > c (pd > c*)
joint(draws)                          # joint probability of the top-k claims

Citation

Calderan, M., Gambarota, F., Finos, L., & Altoè, G. (n.d.). A Prior-Odds Adjustment for the Probability of Direction in Multiple Testing. Retrieved from https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/8zwx2_v2

Run citation("multibayes") in R for the full reference (article and package entries).
